Cyber Attack Disrupts Engineering & Construction Firms Across Turkey

A cyber attack targeting the IT systems of several leading Engineering & Construction firms in Turkey has caused significant disruption to ongoing projects, with operations at sites and offices thrown into disarray. The incident, believed to be a ransomware attack, began on Monday and is ongoing, according to industry sources.

Among the companies affected is Calik Enerji Sanayi Ve Ticaret AS, whose spokesperson confirmed that several core IT systems, including project management and internal communications platforms, have been rendered inaccessible. “Our immediate priority is the safety of our staff and the security of our data,” the spokesperson stated. “We are working with cybersecurity experts to contain the breach and restore our systems.”

Employees at impacted firms reported sudden loss of access to design files, blueprints, and scheduling software. At multiple construction sites, work was temporarily halted as site managers were unable to access digital plans and safety documentation. “The shutdown of our digital systems means we can’t verify certain processes or track progress accurately,” said a site supervisor at the affected Istanbul-based firm Yildirim Proje. “We’ve had to pause some activities until we regain access.”

According to the Turkish Chamber of Civil Engineers, at least seven medium and large Engineering & Construction firms have reported disruptions. “This is a wake-up call for the entire sector,” said Bülent Demir, a board member of the chamber. “Digital infrastructure is now as critical as cranes and concrete. We urge all companies to review their cybersecurity policies as a matter of urgency.”

Union representatives expressed concern about the ongoing uncertainty for workers, with some employees asked to stay home or take on alternative duties while the systems remain down. “We are closely monitoring the situation and advocating for clear communication from employers,” said Özlem Kaya, a spokesperson for a construction workers’ union.

As of Tuesday afternoon, there was no official estimate for when full operations might resume. Authorities have launched an investigation, but details about the perpetrators or demands made have not been disclosed.
